Senses.Explanation: A public case is a recorded encounter or saying of the old masters that is raised and set before someone in public interview. Chan texts themselves compare the term to a government office's case documents, preserving the legal scene while turning it into the tradition's record and test object. Zhongfeng Mingben explicitly says the word is a figure for a government office's case-documents, then says that when a student's understanding cannot be settled, the student brings it before a lineage teacher, who raises a public case to decide it. The Blue Cliff Record preface likewise calls the two graphs clerkly-document language from worldly law and says the patriarchs established such records as public cases for the monasteries. Wumen Huikai says he takes the old men's public cases as tiles for knocking on the gate and guides students according to the occasion. Yuanwu asks whether there was a Chan way before questions, answers, and public cases, then says later people called the old men's occasion-matched pointers public cases. Later records use the term for the seventeen hundred cases, old men's cases that people try to trace line by line, and newly raised interview material. Zen bends legal case-file language into the named record and public-interview object while preserving the legal comparison in its own explanations.
Senses.Note: The headword occurs 3,800 times in 363 allowlisted texts. Eight exact witnesses across six sources clear the highest floor and cover legal self-definition, teacher adjudication, preface, Wumen's gate-tile statement, Yuanwu's historical question, old-case handling, fresh public exchange, and a ready-made case. The headword-absent legal gloss is family evidence. Counted case collections remain deployments of this one record-object, not separate senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 公案乃喻乎公府之案牘也
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhongfeng Mingben, in the Extensive Record of Tianmu Zhongfeng (天目中峰廣錄), explicitly says a public case is a figure for the case-documents of a government office.

Occurrences.Kwic: 學者有所悟解不能自决乃質之於師。則舉公案以决之
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhongfeng Mingben, in the Extensive Record of Tianmu Zhongfeng (天目中峰廣錄), says an unsettled student brings the matter to the teacher, who raises a public case to decide it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 二字乃世間法中吏牘語
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Sanjiao Laoren, in the preface to the Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), calls the two graphs clerkly-document language from worldly law.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖師所以立為公案。留示叢林者
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Sanjiao Laoren, in the preface to the Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), says the patriarchs established these as public cases and left them for the monasteries.

Occurrences.Kwic: 遂將古人公案。作敲門瓦子。隨機引導學者
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wumen Huikai, in The Gateless Barrier (無門關), says he uses the old men's public cases as tiles for knocking on the gate and guides students according to the occasion.

Occurrences.Kwic: 未有問答。未有公案已前。還有禪道麼。古人事不獲已。對機垂示。後人喚作公案。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu Keqin, in the Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), asks about the time before questions, answers, and public cases, then says later people gave the name to the old men's occasion-matched pointers.

Occurrences.Kwic: 禪和子家到處覓相似語，弄聰明求解會，穿鑿穿鑿，將他古人公案事事要問個出跡，句句要討個路頭。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yunxi Langting Ting, in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yunxi Langting Ting (雲溪俍亭挺禪師語錄), describes Chan people trying to trace every old public case and seek a route through every phrase.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：「三百年前舊公案，今日重新意若何？」師云：「蒼海月明光不夜。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Juelang Daosheng, in the Complete Record of Chan Master Juelang Sheng of Tianjie (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄), answers a public question about an old case being renewed today.

Occurrences.Kwic: 未挂古帆，現成公案。由是悟取無悟底面目，迷是不迷底鄉關。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), in the section headed 'Chan Master Furi Weiyue of Jingyin in Kaifeng' (開封淨因佛日惟嶽禪師): Jingyin Weiyue calls the immediately present encounter a ready-made public case before speaking of the face of no-awakening.
